name: THOMPSON, Phillip Bruce, OAM

headline.note: Primary parliamentary chronology now givesArmy2006–2011andSelectability2017–2018; primary first-person account corroborates2011medical discharge over secondary2012claim. JobTrain/APMA/governance/advisory/study roles separated. Unknown hours,leave and pilot-program employer prevent totals; unknown is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Australian Army, 1st Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
career_spells.evidence_note: The Australian of the Year profile says Thompson enlisted at 17 in 2006. His first speech says he was posted to 1 RAR at Townsville that year and deployed to East Timor in 2007 and Afghanistan in 2009. Official member biographies corroborate Army and 1 RAR service. A secondary biographical compilation gives 2006-2012 service, but an exact separation date and primary personnel record were not found. Follow-up: official parliamentary occupation AND military-service sections specify2006–2011; his first-person2025/26welcome also says medical discharge2011. These primary sources supersede secondary2012endpoint, which remains recorded as a conflict rather than discarded silently. No exact separation or medical-leave dates established.
career_spells.counting_note: Public service is established, but exact appointment and separation dates, hours, medical leave and the post-injury service interval are unresolved.

career_spells.employer: Veterans peer-support pilot program, employing entity not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: A contemporaneous Royal Australian Regiment Association director biography says Thompson became manager of a veterans peer-support pilot program in 2015. His official biography more generally says he worked for mental-wellbeing and suicide-prevention organisations after leaving Defence. The program and employing entity, exact start and end, hours and leave are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: Employer and control are unidentified; nonprofit classification cannot be assumed from purpose. No headline calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: The Royal Australian Regiment Association biography says Thompson became a manager of selectability, described as a North Queensland community mental-health organisation, in 2017. Federal Hansard in September 2017 independently identifies him as 'from selectability'. Official biographies say he worked in mental wellbeing and suicide prevention before Parliament. Exact dates, title, hours, leave and campaign arrangements are not published. Official parliamentary biography now resolves title and2017–2018interval; prior2019cutoff replaced. Exact dates/hours/leave and overlap with2018candidacy unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded from public/private headline totals.

career_spells.role: Level 2 pensions and welfare advocate; mental-health and suicide-prevention advocate
career_spells.evidence_note: The Australian of the Year profile describes volunteer listening and veterans' employment, health and wellbeing advocacy. The RAR Association biography identifies Level 2 pensions and welfare advocacy. Sources do not separate paid work from volunteer advocacy across this interval. Prior2019endpoint was not a documented cessation and is removed.
career_spells.counting_note: Only explicitly unpaid or unresolved advocacy is represented here; it is excluded and must not be double-counted with nonprofit employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: The Association's August 2017 national-organisation page and Thompson's official biography identify him as a director. ACNC records confirm the Corporation is a registered charity. Exact appointment and cessation dates, remuneration and workload are not published. Parliamentary biography supplies2016–2019, replacing2017publication observation as start.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit governance is excluded and must not be double-counted as substantive employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: Thompson's official biography lists a directorship of Swiss 8, described as an online suicide-prevention application. Appointment dates, remuneration, workload and overlap with employment are not supplied. Parliamentary biography gives2018–2019. ABR identifies Swiss Technologies Ltd and charity registration28September2018; Swiss8business name9January2019. Registration dates do not define his appointment or prove the whole2018interval had the same legal structure; pre-registration context unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Governance is excluded pending evidence that it was separate substantive paid employment.

career_spells.employer: Bravery Trust, Queensland Day and Australia Day programs; R U OK and Suicide Prevention Australia
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists the three ambassador roles but gives no dates, remuneration or workload. They are retained as unresolved community roles rather than assumed employment. R U OK source and speaker profile identify additional ambassadorships; dates/pay remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Ambassador roles without evidence of substantive paid employment are excluded.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Herbert
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary records show Thompson was elected to the House of Representatives at the 18 May 2019 federal election.

career_spells.employer: JobTrain; exact legal entity to confirm
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary biography gives role and years. Do not conflate Australian JobTrain with US JobTrain Inc or UK recruitment-software company. Legal identity, executive versus governance duties,pay and hours unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Company office represented separately; no evidence of substantive full-time employment. Excluded pending clarification.
